title_as_printed: Isopiestic Molalities of Na2SO4, MgSO4, Na2SO4-MgSO4, and KCl at 25 C

footnotes_as_printed.a: Saturated solution in equilibrium with solid KCl.
footnotes_as_printed.b: Saturated solution in equilibrium with MgSO4.7H2O.
footnotes_as_printed.c: Saturated solution in equilibrium with Na2SO4.10H2O.

pressure_note: not stated (isopiestic equilibrium at the equilibrium water vapour pressure; no pressure reported)

value.what: molality of the test solution isopiestic with the KCl standard in the same row

value2.what: molality of the KCl isopiestic reference solution

phi.what: osmotic coefficient of the KCl standard calculated by the authors from published equations (refs 6, 7)

composition.other_species: mixture column: equimolal Na2SO4 + MgSO4 (ratio of molalities 1/0.999998); the printed m is taken as the molality of each salt (nu = 5 ions per formula pair in eq 1, inferred); water is the solvent

extra_unmapped: Phi, KCl is the standard's osmotic coefficient (authors' calculation from literature equations)
conversion_needs: molality-of-mixture convention (each salt vs total) should be confirmed from eq 1
notes: 62 data rows printed and written. Each row is one isopiestic equilibrium; empty cells = that test solution not present in that equilibrium. Rows 0 (KCl, a), 20 (MgSO4, b) and 42 (Na2SO4, c) are saturated-solution (solubility) points: KCl 4.8088, MgSO4.7H2O 3.0211, Na2SO4.10H2O 1.9526 mol/kg; footnote letters moved to the note column. Measurements for Na2SO4 and MgSO4 extend into the supersaturated region.
hold_table: the table prints no osmotic coefficient of the test salts (Phi, KCl is the standard's literature-derived coefficient); test-salt phi is derivable only by eq 1, phi = nu* m* phi*/(nu m); wide per-column layout not readable by the builder (audit 2026-10-02)
